title: Build a depth-independent rig debug view for skeleton inspection
description:
## Summary
Extend skeleton display into a usable SceneView rig-debug presentation so pose, topology, and weighting changes can be inspected without navigating generated Unity hierarchy.

## Explicit anatomy requirement
The debug workflow must remain generic: it must not assume biped, quadruped, legs, or a fixed limb count. Any articulated limb chain must be discoverable, selectable, labeled, and focusable through structural skeleton metadata rather than PartType-specific branches.

## Current implementation
`RigDebugView` provides x-ray visibility, adjustable bone width, selected-bone emphasis, click selection, semantic labels plus stable IDs, whole-skeleton/selected-chain/body/limb/selected-bone focus, and snapshot-based chain discovery. It uses the live `CreatureRig.RestSkeleton` and indexed transforms rather than re-resolving editor-session DNA. `CreatureRig` also exposes `TryGetBone` and a read-only map boundary.

## Acceptance
- Bones remain visible through the generated mesh.
- Skeleton, selected chain, body, all articulated limbs, and selected bone can be framed directly.
- Selected bones are distinguishable by shape/thickness as well as color.
- Machine IDs and semantic display names are available.
- Focus behavior is based on the live generated rig, not stale editor state.
- A selected terminal child frames its owning articulated parent chain rather than forcing hierarchy traversal.
- No biped/quadruped/leg-count assumption is encoded in the debug view.
- Manual Unity SceneView validation is still required before closure.

## Scope limits
Do not move morphology topology, weighting ownership, or foot-grounding logic into this task. Full mesh suppression and pose-preview controls remain deferred until the basic debug presentation is visually validated.

## Status
InProgress: generic implementation landed; Unity visual validation remains open.

## Evidence
See the skeleton/animation visualization, implementation delta, and next-round audit documents under `docs/audits/` on branch `audit/skeleton-animation-improvements-2026-09-07`.

## Latest implementation note
`Frame Selected Chain` now walks the live skeleton parent links from the selected bone to the first Body-rooted ancestor and supplements that with the selected articulated part's segment bones. This makes child geometry such as feet/hands practical to inspect without a special-case leg workflow.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Sequential implementation rounds completed: standalone x-ray SceneView rig overlay, adjustable thickness, semantic labels plus IDs, direct selection, skeleton/chain/body/leg/selected-bone framing, and live-snapshot ownership. Unity visual validation remains the closure gate.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Generalized the debug presentation to the same arbitrary-limb invariant as runtime rigging: removed the hard-coded Focus Legs control and PartType.Leg/Foot label filter. `Focus Limbs` now discovers articulated bones structurally via segment/attachment metadata, so wings, arms, tentacles, antennae, multiple leg sets, and other supported chains do not require new editor modes.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Follow-up UX hardening: `Frame Selected Chain` now traverses live parent links so selecting a terminal child such as a foot/hand includes its owning articulated chain. The implementation remains structural and does not depend on PartType or a fixed limb count.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Audit synthesis 2026-09-07: pull the deferred raw generated mesh presentation into this owner. `CreaturePreviewController.BindImplicitSurface` destroys the preview-root `MeshFilter` and `MeshRenderer` before creating the skinned path, and neither preview path exposes a raw/rest-mesh toggle. Add a structural presentation mode that can show the generated mesh without `SkinnedMeshRenderer`, while preserving the current debug view's generic arbitrary-limb behavior. Acceptance must include a Unity SceneView check that toggles raw versus skinned display and confirms the two paths do not create duplicate owned objects. Provenance: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-rig-liveuse-audit-2026-09-07.md`, Finding 4.
